source_text:
ἐν κόλποις Ἀβραὰμ πένης ἀναπαυόμενος, πρὸ τῆς παρουσίας τοῦ Σωτῆρος καὶ πρὸ
τῆς συντελείας τοῦ αἰῶνος, καὶ διὰ τοῦτο πρὸ τῆς ἀναστάσεως λεγόμενοι ὁ μὲν ἐν
ᾅδου κολάζεσθαι, ὁ δὲ ἐν κόλποις Ἀβραὰμ ἀναπαύεσθαι, διδάσκουσιν ὅτι καὶ νῦν τῇ
ἀπαλλαγῇ σώματι χρῆται ἡ ψυχή. Ἐκ τῶν Μεθοδίου. Φράσας (Ὠριγένης)
pass_a_gloss: poor man resting in the bosom of Abraham, before the presence of the Savior and before the consummation of the age, and on that account before the resurrection said—the one to be punished in Hades, the other to rest in Abraham's bosom—teach that even now at the departure the soul uses a body. From the things of Methodius. Having phrased (Origen)
pass_b_english: …poor man resting in Abraham's bosom—spoken of before the Savior's coming, before the world's consummation, and so before the resurrection—the one punished in Hades, the other at rest in Abraham's bosom—teach that even now, at departure, the soul uses a body.
From Methodius. Origen, having put it this way…

choices.choice: PG 11 De Resurrectione (Khazarzar); locked rem mid Greek.
Parable scene is pre-parousia and pre-resurrection; soul still body-using.
From Methodius; Origen continues into close.
